1. Repeated pauses create false stop events 📘 Rule violation ⌂ Architecture
>
>Description >
> >
>PlaybookEngine.pause() passes quiet=True for an already paused pipeline, but stop() still
>appends pipeline.stop_suppressed before checking that flag. A repeated pause therefore creates a
>suppressed-stop record even though the pause is meant to be a no-op, affecting the inbox and stop
>history without notifying the operator.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/playbook.py[R3478-3480]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/8/files#diff-d4c45908377a317f0fbbccad6f8af7a74c4af564c4272d3cecc7126bf1be9204R3478-R3480) > >```diff >+ # §44 rule 3: over a human pause too, a no-op that keeps `paused_by` and the >+ # kept ends, and is not a stop: never notified, never the suppressed mark. >+ await self.stop(PAUSE_REASON, {"by": "hands pause" if by == "cli" else by}, quiet=True) >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>The implementation contradicts the explicit DESIGN no-op rule and creates observable false stop
>history.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>DESIGN.md specifies that a pause over an existing human pause is a no-op, not a stop, and must not
>be notified. The changed pause() implementation passes quiet=True, but the paused branch appends
>pipeline.stop_suppressed before using quiet to suppress only the mark and notification.
>
> > Rule 3263077: [Code must conform to DESIGN.md unless explicitly excepted in FINDINGS.md](https://app.qodo.ai/rules/3263077?state=active) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[3429-3441\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L3429-L3441) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[3477-3483\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L3477-L3483) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A pause over an existing human pause is intended to be a no-op, but the current `quiet=True` path still appends `pipeline.stop_suppressed` before suppressing notification and state updates. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/playbook.py[3429-3441] >- src/hands/playbook.py[3477-3483] > >## Recommended Fix >Handle `quiet` before appending the `pipeline.stop_suppressed` event in the already-paused branch, or return from the quiet human-pause path before recording any suppressed-stop event. Preserve the existing no-op behavior by leaving the pause, kept ends, and suppressed-stop mark unchanged, while still checking the at-rest condition. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

2. Decided jobs receive late hold notices 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>Api.send and _publish_held await held-reason computation, then announce a hold without
>rechecking the job’s gate or current state. If another client approves or denies the job during that
>wait, the later notification describes a hold that no longer exists and can create new approval
>buttons.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/api.py[R446-447]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/8/files#diff-16f021e493ba18b1e5f11a7ee4f78300324921ac8ae5a15bbe45cab098c59139R446-R447) > >```diff >+ await self.daemon.decide_held_reason(job) > self.spool.append_event( >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Accepted hold-publication fixes show this team prioritizes correct asynchronous hold notifications
>and startup publication paths.
>
> > [PR-#7](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/7) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Gated jobs start held, but a gate decision can move them out of that state. In Api.send, the new
>await precedes an unconditional job.held event whose listener creates hold actions without
>rechecking the job; at startup, the socket is already listening when _publish_held snapshots held
>jobs, awaits each reason, and publishes hold notifications and actions from those snapshots.
>
> > [src/hands/daemon.py\[568-580\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/daemon.py/#L568-L580) > [src/hands/api.py\[440-451\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/api.py/#L440-L451) > [src/hands/api.py\[1438-1483\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/api.py/#L1438-L1483) > [src/hands/daemon.py\[881-899\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/daemon.py/#L881-L899) > [src/hands/daemon.py\[268-297\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/daemon.py/#L268-L297) > [src/hands/daemon.py\[424-451\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/daemon.py/#L424-L451) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A client can approve or deny a held job while `Api.send` or startup hold publication awaits reason computation, leaving a stale hold event or notification to be published. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/api.py[440-451] >- src/hands/daemon.py[424-428] >- src/hands/daemon.py[430-451] >- src/hands/daemon.py[901-912] > >## Recommended Fix >After reason computation, reload the job before filing `job.held` or publishing a startup hold. File the event only if the gate is still pending, and publish the startup hold only if the job is still held; keep the startup list consistent with that check and clear any cached reason when the gate has already been decided. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

3. Restarts can miss the quiet moment 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>check_at_rest runs when a pause is sent or a job ends, but startup does not run it for a restored
>human pause after resolving pending retries. If a pending limited job is not rescheduled and all
>persisted jobs are terminal, the unset at-rest mark has no subsequent job transition to trigger the
>notification.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/playbook.py[R3575-3582]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/8/files#diff-d4c45908377a317f0fbbccad6f8af7a74c4af564c4272d3cecc7126bf1be9204R3575-R3582) > >```diff >+ if not self.human_paused or self.state.at_rest is not None: >+ return >+ busy = [job.id for job in self.spool.list_jobs() if job.state not in TERMINAL_STATES] >+ if busy: >+ log.debug("playbook: not at rest: job(s) %s not ended", ", ".join(busy)) >+ return >+ if self.limits is not None and self.limits.resume_scheduled(): >+ log.debug("playbook: not at rest: a §6 resume is scheduled") >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Startup can permanently miss the promised at-rest notification when no later transition occurs.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The at-rest mark is persisted, but the new check is invoked only at pause and terminal-job edges.
>Startup can skip a pending limited job at max_resumes and contains no at-rest check afterward.
>
> > [src/hands/playbook.py\[1609-1612\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L1609-L1612) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[1934-1942\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L1934-L1942) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[3478-3487\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L3478-L3487) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[3566-3589\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L3566-L3589) > [src/hands/daemon.py\[283-300\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/daemon.py/#L283-L300) > [src/hands/limits.py\[415-442\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/limits.py/#L415-L442) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Restoring an idle human pause does not announce rest when startup declines to reschedule its pending limit retry. >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/daemon.py[283-300] >- src/hands/playbook.py[3566-3589] >## Recommended Fix >After startup restores and reconciles jobs and pending limit retries, call `check_at_rest` for the restored pause. Preserve the persisted mark so an already-announced pause is not announced twice. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

4. A failed retry hides the quiet moment 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>check_at_rest excludes a pause while a limit-resume task is scheduled, but nothing checks again
>when _resume_after fails without creating a job. If the retry fails while no other job is active,
>its suppressed stop is announced but the human never receives the at-rest notification for that
>pause.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/playbook.py[R3581-3583]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/8/files#diff-d4c45908377a317f0fbbccad6f8af7a74c4af564c4272d3cecc7126bf1be9204R3581-R3583) > >```diff >+ if self.limits is not None and self.limits.resume_scheduled(): >+ log.debug("playbook: not at rest: a §6 resume is scheduled") >+ return >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>A failed scheduled retry leaves the at-rest predicate stale despite the pause remaining active.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The new predicate blocks publication while any retry task is unfinished. The retry's exception path
>calls stop and finishes without a job-end callback or another at-rest check.
>
> > [src/hands/playbook.py\[3575-3589\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L3575-L3589) > [src/hands/limits.py\[399-402\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/limits.py/#L399-L402) > [src/hands/limits.py\[464-476\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/limits.py/#L464-L476) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[3429-3440\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L3429-L3440) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A limit retry that fails without starting a job removes the reason for withholding `hands: at rest`, but creates no job end to recheck it. >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/limits.py[464-476] >- src/hands/playbook.py[3575-3589] >## Recommended Fix >Recheck at-rest eligibility after a scheduled retry terminates without starting a job, once that task no longer counts as scheduled. Retain the existing suppression and notification for its stop. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/0508e1a9-3415-4416-83ec-f491e2955141?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/0508e1a9-3415-4416-83ec-f491e2955141)
5. Nested builders miss a playbook warning 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>_owner_warning joins the repository-relative configured playbook path to its repo argument, but
>daemon-side kit filing passes the builder's working directory rather than the repository root. When
>that directory is below the root and the kit changes a custom-path playbook, the check looks beneath
>the directory twice and can omit the warning that the current autonomous playbook requires human
>ownership.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/kit.py[R913-917]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/8/files#diff-c741f63d4fccb12bbfc566ee658f6a10d5d610c9e09e4a336f11292aaa5c1b37R913-R917) > >```diff >+ candidates = [*([configured] if configured is not None else []), *PLAYBOOK_PATHS] >+ present = [name for name in dict.fromkeys(candidates) if (repo / name).is_file()] >+ for name in present: > with contextlib.suppress(PlaybookError, OSError): >- if _load((repo / present[0]).read_bytes(), present[0]).architect_is_autonomous: >- autonomous.append(f"the repository's {present[0]}") >- with contextlib.suppress(PlaybookError): >- if _load(kit.files[carried[0]], carried[0]).architect_is_autonomous: >- autonomous.append(f"the kit's {carried[0]}") >+ if _load((repo / name).read_bytes(), name).architect_is_autonomous: >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>This is a deterministic nested-path bug causing a required warning to be omitted.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>playbook_repo_path prepends the builder cwd's Git prefix, while _file_kit passes that cwd as
>repo. The added candidate read consequently repeats the prefix for nested builders.
>
> > [src/hands/playbook.py\[694-709\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L694-L709) > [src/hands/api.py\[823-827\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/api.py/#L823-L827) > [src/hands/kit.py\[909-924\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/kit.py/#L909-L924) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The configured playbook path includes the builder directory's Git prefix, while daemon-side checks use that directory as their repository argument. >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/kit.py[877-889] >- src/hands/kit.py[909-918] >- src/hands/api.py[823-827] >## Recommended Fix >Resolve the repository-relative configured path against the actual Git root, or derive a path relative to the supplied check directory. Cover a builder cwd below the root with a configured custom playbook path. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/edf2367a-322f-49a3-89a7-631f50453b68?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/edf2367a-322f-49a3-89a7-631f50453b68)
6. Ends arriving after a refused resume are lost 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>resume calls _load(stop_on_error=False), and a failed load sets self.playbook = None before it
>returns, while the human pause stays. After that, _under_human_pause returns early on `book is
>None, so a builder/aux/driver end that arrives later is neither kept nor notified, and resume`
>rules on orphaned or failed jobs stop firing; the next successful resume then has nothing to
>replay.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/playbook.py[R3503-3508]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/8/files#diff-d4c45908377a317f0fbbccad6f8af7a74c4af564c4272d3cecc7126bf1be9204R3503-R3508) > >```diff >+ problem = await self._load(stop_on_error=False) >+ if problem is not None: >+ raise ResumeRefused( >+ f"{problem}; the human pause and its {len(self.state.kept)} kept end(s) stay " >+ "until a `resume` whose playbook loads (§44)" >+ ) >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>A refused resume silently drops later role ends, directly violating the documented
>pause-and-kept-ends guarantee.
>
> > [PR-#6](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/6) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>_load assigns self.playbook = None inside the except PlaybookError branch before it checks
>stop_on_error, so a refused resume replaces the previously loaded playbook with None. Because it
>isn't a stop, nothing is notified and suppressed_stop isn't set. _under_human_pause returns with
>only a log line whenever book is None, which skips _keep for ROLE_ENDS. resume is not limited
>to the at-rest moment, so a job still running (for example, a mission-long builder job) can end in
>this window and its end is dropped. The docs promise that 'nothing is silent' and that 'the pause
>and its kept ends stay'.
>
> > [src/hands/playbook.py\[1811-1843\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L1811-L1843) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2064-2068\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2064-L2068) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[3500-3518\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L3500-L3518) > [docs/PLAYBOOK.md\[361-369\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/docs/PLAYBOOK.md/#L361-L369) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >When a human pause's `resume` is refused because the playbook does not load, `_load(stop_on_error=False)` has already set `self.playbook = None`. Under the still-active human pause, `_under_human_pause` returns early when `book is None`, so role ends that arrive afterwards are neither kept nor notified, and `resume` rules no longer fire. The series' next step can be lost without anyone being told. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/playbook.py[1811-1843] >- src/hands/playbook.py[3500-3518] >- src/hands/playbook.py[2064-2068] > >## Recommended Fix >With `stop_on_error=False`, leave `self.playbook` (and preferably `self.load_error`) as they were when the load fails, so the engine keeps deciding with the playbook loaded before the refused resume. One way: in `_load`, assign `self.playbook = None` / `self.load_error` only when `stop_on_error` is True, or save and restore them in `resume()` around the refused load. Separately, consider keeping a ROLE_ENDS end in `_under_human_pause` when a playbook file exists but failed to load (`self.load_error is not None`), rather than dropping it. Add a test: pause, refused resume, then a `builder.done` arrives and must be kept. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/3eb6b97c-36f6-42c0-bf51-ca8683747def?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/3eb6b97c-36f6-42c0-bf51-ca8683747def)
7. Owner kits suggest a refused command 🔗 Cross-repo conflict ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>_under_human_pause fires Discotrade’s builder.done kit-applied notification immediately, leaving
>its instruction to send go unchanged. When an owner decisions kit finishes during a human pause,
>go is refused until the operator sends resume.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/playbook.py[R2082-2083]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/8/files#diff-d4c45908377a317f0fbbccad6f8af7a74c4af564c4272d3cecc7126bf1be9204R2082-R2083) > >```diff >+ if chosen is not None and then == "notify": >+ await self._fire(chosen, event, job, match) >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●● Moderate` > >
>The conflict is plausible, but cross-repository kit instructions make team disposition uncertain.
>
> > [PR-#6](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/6) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The PR fires notify rules during a human pause and refuses go under that pause; Discotrade’s
>matching kit-applied rule instructs the operator to send go.
>
> > [hands -> discotrade](https://app.qodo.ai/management/relationships?repoId=77e6b9e3-9009-4fbe-bd8c-e1c4bd92a98f&relatedRepoId=f8bc154f-fef0-4515-a253-775ba818fa12&view=table) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2081-2085\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2081-L2085) > [src/hands/api.py\[537-540\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/8453b8a046986edf29f2127aa7f816a6779011f5/src/hands/api.py/#L537-L540) > [External repo: SigorMatt/discotrade, PLAYBOOK.toml \[35-42\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/discotrade/blob/ed08ffa00d56ad063a8f792716f036290b792a1d/PLAYBOOK.toml/#L35-L42) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Discotrade’s kit-applied notification tells operators to send `go`, but a kit applied during a human pause leaves `go` refused until `resume`. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- /cross_repos/discotrade/PLAYBOOK.toml[35-42] >- src/hands/playbook.py[2081-2085] > >## Recommended Fix >Update Discotrade’s notification to say to send `resume` first if the pipeline is human-paused, and otherwise send `go`. Keep the immediate notification behavior in hands. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
